behaviors.protocol_context: cluster, current term, applied voting membership
behaviors.trigger: Leader proposal or peer replication response; follower Replicate request
implementation_guards: Proposal rejected during leadership transfer; at most one pending config change proposal is retained.
Follower requires matching predecessor term; conflicts at or below committed panic.
Leader aggregates only remotes and witnesses; commit requires selected index term equals current term.
writes: Entry term/index assigned; follower suffix merged; remote match updated; log.committed advanced monotonically.
external_effects: Replicate and ReplicateResp messages; commit changes broadcast to peers.
important_branches: Rejected replication decreases next and retries; heartbeat response resumes waiting remote and sends missing suffix.
Single voter can commit on append; observers replicate but do not contribute to commit quorum.

behaviors.protocol_context: cluster term, role, leader identity and voting population
behaviors.trigger: Election timeout, RequestVote/response, higher-term message, same-term leader message to candidate, quorum check or transfer
implementation_guards: Election blocked while committed entries exceed applied; witnesses/observers do not campaign.
Vote requires eligible prior vote and up-to-date last log term/index; observer vote replies are excluded and votes deduplicated.
Lower-term messages ignored; higher-term RequestVote may be ignored within check-quorum lease unless transfer hint; network responses from unknown participants rejected by Peer.Handle.
writes: Reset term/vote when term changes; clear pending readIndex, votes, transfer and remote progress on reset; retain log and committed prefix.
New leader appends current-term no-op and reconstructs pending config status from log.
external_effects: Vote messages, replication after election; TimeoutNow only to known full voter caught up to leader last index.
important_branches: CheckQuorum steps down on insufficient active voters; transfer blocks proposals and times out.
Forwarded proposal/read requests are termless; normal outgoing protocol responses carry sender term.

Leader promotion scans configuration changes only above committed; the normal campaign path first blocks whenever committed exceeds explicitly notified applied index. This makes omitted committed-but-unapplied entries a guarded precondition in the traced normal election/TimeoutNow path.

cross_activity_effects.A1: New-term support is reconstructed rather than carrying remote matches/votes over; preserved committed history constrains future candidates.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Unconfirmed readIndex state is discarded on reset; client timeout remains separate.

behaviors.execution_owner: leader handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation and follower read response handler

writes: Receiver adds ReadyToRead using received message context and LogIndex.
external_effects: Local statuses use s.ctx; remote statuses send to s.from but encode the triggering heartbeat context m.Hint/m.HintHigh.

StateMachine.Handle defers node.StepReady when a task was popped, including paths whose individual entry callback is ignored. handle advances visible lastApplied after each entry task, and node.handleEvents consumes the latest applied index and checks pending reads. Thus a missing per-entry read callback does not alone establish a lost wakeup.

facts.meaning: This local log has a monotonically established committed prefix ending at committed; ordinary leader advancement uses current-term quorum replication, follower advancement uses leader propagation, and restore/startup provide separate history paths.
facts.validity_context: Local entryLog including its snapshot boundary, across term transitions; not a statement that all entries have been applied.
facts.durability: In-memory until update persistence; log/state saved by engine before normal acknowledgements.
facts.recovery: Loaded from persisted State with range checks or restored snapshot.

facts.meaning: A pending read status is included in the queue prefix released by confirmation of a queued context after sufficient distinct recorded confirmations plus the leader; its original source and context remain in the returned status, while its index is raised to that of the confirmed context.
facts.validity_context: One leader readIndex instance after current-term commitment check for multi-voter admission; queue entries are volatile and discarded on reset.
facts.recovery: No restoration; reset creates empty readIndex.

Disk snapshot recovery and transport completion interleavings need deeper examination beyond representative install path.

Session history stores sm.Result by value and client result delivery copies that value without cloning Data. Does the caller or state-machine contract permit later byte-slice mutation, or is ownership transferred/read-only? Client ProposalCompleted duties constrain legal retry histories and must be retained before any cache-integrity claim.

formation.explanation: Peer routes proposals to leader. Leader assigns term/index, appends, and sends predecessor-qualified replication; followers match predecessor and protect committed history. Acknowledgements update per-peer matches; majority of full voters and witnesses selects an index whose term must equal current leader term. Commit is propagated via replication and bounded heartbeat commit. Engine persists state and entries before acknowledgement messages, and queues committed entries according to FastApply durability overlap. RSM applies entries and membership, then node callbacks report proposal/read completion. Rejection responses retry earlier suffix; compaction selects snapshot for active peers.

context.explanation: Election timers initiate campaign only for eligible full voters without committed-but-unapplied work. New term resets transient votes/progress/read confirmations; vote granting checks log freshness and prior vote, and candidate forms authority from deduplicated quorum replies. Higher-term protocol messages normally cause stepdown, with check-quorum vote suppression exception; lower terms are ignored. Same-term leader messages demote candidates. Quorum checks, removal and transfer govern loss/change of leadership. Transfer waits for target catchup and triggers target election via TimeoutNow, while blocking proposals until completion or timeout.

connection.explanation: Terms qualify newly counted support, but established committed history survives authority reset and constrains future logs and votes. Membership becomes active through RSM application; campaign defers when applied state lags commit, so a new leader does not simply form using its old unapplied membership. New leader reconstructs pending config status and commits a current-term no-op before multi-voter ReadIndex admission. Pending read contexts are reset with authority; within one leader context, voter heartbeat confirmation releases queue prefixes for local readiness or forwarded replies, and clients require exact context plus applied index. Old network responses are term-filtered and unknown responders rejected; pending client work may independently drop or timeout.

open_details: Forwarded queue-prefix release routes each response using the confirming heartbeat context, while local readiness uses per-status context; application/client endpoint consequences and other authority contexts remain separate questions.
Disk/concurrent state machine crash/recovery, storage implementations, session deduplication and membership-change message interleavings remain deeper variants.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority changes, stale-work handling and their persistence/membership/application connections have been traced. Local read-response correlation and deeper fault variants remain questions, not unexplained core ownership.
